title: GEMM dispatch orchestration and ABI stability for mixed CUTLASS/CUDA stacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We observe sporadic startup latency spikes and occasional incorrect kernel selection when heterogeneous hosts run mixed CUTLASS/CUDA/Triton stacks. Root causes include symbol-version mismatch between CUTLASS releases, opportunistic GEMM probe ordering that returns non-optimal kernels for common shapes, and lacking an orchestration layer to normalise dispatch decisions across runtime variants. This leads to 95th/99th tail regressions under bursty workloads and makes safe rolling upgrades brittle.

Goal: Implement a lightweight GEMM dispatch orchestration and ABI stability harness that: (1) normalises kernel symbol mapping across CUTLASS versions, (2) centralises gemm-probe ordering with deterministic tie-breakers and preheat paths, (3) provides signed kernel manifest verification for safer rollouts, and (4) adds CI/bench coverage for mixed-version fuzz and tail-latency regression guards.

Planned deliverables:
- design doc with dispatch rules and ABI mapping table (linked below)
- runtime shim to translate symbol names and export a stable dispatch facade
- preheat path to warm the fast GEMM kernels for common shapes during warmup window
- signed kernel manifest + verification flow and package format changes for cutlass bundles
- CI matrix jobs to run mixed CUTLASS/CUDA/Triton combinations and a deterministic probe fuzz harness
- rollout plan: canary on dedicated pool -> gradual ramp with performance SLO gates -> full rollout

Trade-offs and notes:
- Extra layer adds code surface and small dispatch latency (~50-150us) for first-call mapping; mitigated by preheat and caching.
- The signed manifest requires release pipeline changes and artifact signing keys (coord with release eng).
- Fallback slow-path retained for safety; all mappings are revocable by manifest version in case of regression.

References and artifacts:
- Design/Spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/GPU/GEMM+Dispatch+Orchestration+Spec (internal)
- Prototype PR with proof-of-concept shim + tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/3456
- Bench dashboard (canary vs baseline): https://internal.dashboards.redwood.ai/boards/bench/gemm-dispatch-2026-03-08
- Incident notes (startup tail regressions): https://drive.redwood.ai/incident/INC-2026-0112-gemm-probe

Acceptance criteria:
- CI passes mixed-version matrix for 3 consecutive runs without probe flakiness
- End-to-end canary shows <=3% perf regression on p50 and >6% improvement on p99 compared to current slow-path in our workload profiles OR no worse than baseline and no functional failures
- Signed manifest flow validated in staging and signing keys provisioned for release pipeline

Rollout steps (high level):
1) Merge runtime shim behind feature flag and add probe telemetry
2) Run canary on small dedicated pool (internal only) for 48 hours, collect SLOs and trace samples
3) If canary passes, progressively increase to 10% then 50% with automatic rollback on SLA breach
4) Full rollout once 7-day stability is confirmed
